runs.title: Bootstrap evidence pass for Jev
runs.summary: First source-led catalogue of Jev use cases, open-source substitutions, directly evidenced projects, and dated access/pricing routes.

runs.title: Access, pricing, and availability refresh for Jev
runs.summary: Current official Jev model, endpoint, aliases, price, limits, text-only input, access ambiguity, legal/data terms, OpenRouter and Cloudflare routes, inaccessible Vercel status, and the independent proxy price were checked; remaining account and gateway gaps stay explicit.

runs.title: Alternatives verification refresh (local-only)
runs.summary: A local-artifact-only refresh of the six named alternatives retained direct URLs and substitution layers, upgraded no row, marked all current project facts unknown, and made the no-verified-open-weight-Jev finding explicit without implying that none exists.

runs.title: Alternatives substitution matrix refresh
runs.summary: Direct-source audit of exactly six named alternatives, separating model parity, System One-like interface, local/privacy boundary, workflow role, and trade-offs; no verified open-weight Jev model was found.

runs.title: Bounded adoption and product verification audit
runs.summary: Direct-source audit of killmyidea, Jev Showcase, the TypeSafe playground router, jev-usecases, and the Awesome Jev lead index. killmyidea is a direct-source application with public-deployment metadata but unverified public access and adoption; the other leads remain an unofficial integration, an explicitly mocked demo, an MIT reference harness, or an index. No verified production product was found.

runs.title: Builder fit and maintenance synthesis
runs.summary: The 24 September synthesis added a pilot, route fallback, substitute, wait, and stop branch; preserved bounded no-verified-open-weight-Jev and no-verified-production-product findings; proposed source refresh rules; and recorded that no independent workload measurement was run.

runs.title: Bounded freshness and change-detection pass
runs.summary: Corrected the independent proxy tier record, recorded the MCA displayed Sep 23 update with exact diff unknown, dated the waitlist observation, and preserved older source-check dates and bounded negative findings.

runs.title: Support-ticket workload-evaluation protocol
runs.summary: Prepared an unfilled Choice evaluation method for one support-ticket route. It separates consecutive and challenge cohorts, freezes labels and comparators, includes review and failure accounting, and records that no Jev call or measured result occurred.

runs.title: Full Jev catalogue rebuild and 24-hour monitor
runs.summary: Direct-source rebuild of use cases, independent Jev-like alternatives, project integrations, route pricing and access; no production product or independent benchmark verified. Monitored the preceding 24 hours with documented platform gaps.

runs.title: Second full-scope Jev source pass
runs.summary: Expanded projects, use cases and layered alternatives; corrected Vercel Free promotion boundary and monitored exact preceding 24 hours. No authenticated call, independent benchmark or verified production deployment.

runs.title: Post-promotion route and comparison check
runs.summary: Vercel still displayed Free after its stated 25 Sep promotion end; effective Jev rate unknown. Cloudflare listed $0.042/M input and zero output/cached input. Added Opper route and one operator-reported Jev–Kev suite; narrowed Laya and JevAny artifact boundaries.

runs.title: Seven-day Jev access checkpoint and daily discovery
runs.summary: Vercel now shows rounded $0.04/M input instead of its 26 Sep Free display; exact tariff, Jev free-credit eligibility and bill unverified. Other route lists rechecked; QuantDinger documented as optional fail-open integration, not verified live operation.

runs.title: Jev implementation-path audit and daily discovery
runs.summary: Source-path audit of Jevmail, WordPress comment triage and QuantDinger distinguishes error, no-key and bypass policies from observed production use; no exact-time new item verified in the bounded 27–28 September monitor. Route lists showed no material established change.

runs.title: Release 1 question pages: access, cost, trust, build, limits and videos
runs.summary: Checked signup and credit status (reopened 27 Sep, no new-user credit), route prices and limits, lookalike resellers (3–16× list price), billing basis and third-party token counts, production claims, the Python SDK, error codes, confidence semantics, 17 documented limitations, 46 demo videos and new alternatives. Corrected two wrongly 'official' project labels. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Integration trust: Claude Code and MCP guardrails, TypeScript paths and testing without a key
runs.summary: Read the failure paths of five Claude Code, MCP and agent-guard integrations at pinned commits and the official plugin in full: only LangChain AutoModeMiddleware fails closed, two ship in shadow or log-only mode, one is advisory and one fails open. Compared four TypeScript paths, twelve no-key test facilities and ten failure branches; ran one hook and one retry client offline. Corrected the oh-my-claudecode timeout note and the jev-mcp product row; access and price fields unchanged. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Evaluation evidence and home status: graded benchmarks, terms and access
runs.summary: Graded 14 published Jev studies read at their primary source and 10 shorter rows (A–D with flags; all results Reported, none run by the pool) and recomputed one study's published log offline. TypeSafe's MCA barred publishing benchmarks until its 19 Sep 2026 version; the current terms have no such clause. Set out 10 criteria for Jev vs an LLM vs a classifier. Home status: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational (console HTTP 403, signup not observed). Rate limits changed to 100K tokens/s and 40 requests/s. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Laya vs Kev, data handling by route, and support-ticket triage
runs.summary: Compared hosted Jev, Laya and Kev on the same rows: only Opper's 362-item test finds an open model (Kev-4B) within noise of Jev, and JevBench scores Laya and earlier Kev previews well below Jev. Quoted training, retention and ZDR terms for TypeSafe direct and four gateways with gateway and provider layers apart: no primary text allows training on prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and monitor for fraud and abuse; Vercel also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, marked not ZDR. Read five ticket-triage projects in source: four send unsure tickets to a person, one archives tickets on API errors. Access unchanged; rate-limit change narrowed. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Model routing, the jev-mcp version check, and content moderation
runs.summary: Read OpenRouter's Jev Router docs (failure, long-context and routed-model billing not documented) and six self-hosted Jev routers at pinned commits: one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model, five keep the current model, pick locally or choose no model. @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.12.0 and 0.13.0 keep the audited failure path. Read six moderation projects at pinned commits: four leave the post up when Jev fails, one holds it, one returns no decision; no published moderation accuracy found. Access unchanged. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Email and lead sorting, oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0, Products refresh and n8n nodes
runs.summary: Read five email and lead sorters at pinned commits: none changes the mailbox when Jev errors; of the 3 that can write to the mailbox, only 1 sends unsure mail to a Review label. oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0 keeps its failure path; its default timeout is now 2,000 ms. Products ledger now 61 rows, 39 grade A, none independently verified in production. TypeSafe's own n8n node is the scoped @typesafe-ai package; all 5 nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error by default. Listed request limit now 80 per second; access unchanged. No pool Jev call.

runs.title: Trading and fraud gates, the failure checklist and Jev as a judge
runs.summary: Read four Jev trading bots and three fraud or payment gates at pinned commits: 2 of the 4 bots can still place a new order when Jev errors, all 4 can trade without Jev, and none of the 3 gates has a payment call site. Recomputed failure behaviour across 39 implementations in 7 use cases: on a Jev error 21 stop or hold the action and 5 let it through unchecked. Read four Jev judge tools: DeepEval stops the run on a Jev error; the other 3 drop the item from the score, and openlayer jevals still reports it as passed. Products: 67 rows, 47 grade A, none independently verified. TypeSafe lists 6 subprocessors (Nebius and CoreWeave added 2 Oct). Access unchanged. No pool Jev call, trade, payment or eval.

runs.title: Browser and computer use, framework integrations, and Jev on Bedrock or Azure
runs.summary: Read 7 Jev browser and computer-use agents at pinned commits: none clicks or types when Jev errors, but 5 act on low-confidence answers and only 1 asks a person before send, buy or delete. Read 6 Jev framework packages: 4 are pre-1.0 and none comes from TypeSafe; 4 raise Jev errors to the caller, while the community Spring AI filter and the LlamaIndex reranker fail open. Jev is not listed in the Amazon Bedrock or Azure AI Foundry model catalogs (5 Oct, 05:18–05:19 UTC). Failure checklist: 51 implementations in 9 use cases; 30 stop or hold the action on a Jev error and 6 let it through unchecked. Products: 72 rows, 55 grade A, none independently verified. Access unchanged. No pool Jev call, agent run or install.

runs.title: Coding agents beyond Claude Code, and Jev model IDs and aliases by route
runs.summary: Read 18 Jev integrations for Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent at pinned commits: 1 is vendor-published (OpenClaw) and none comes from TypeSafe; 6 act on Jev's answer, and 4 of those let the tool call run when Jev errors. Read model IDs and aliases on 6 routes: 4 accept a versioned ID; Vercel and Cloudflare take only an unversioned one; jev-latest points to jev-1.13.0. Failure checklist: 58 implementations in 10 use cases; 32 stop or hold the action on a Jev error and 7 let it through unchecked. Products: 92 rows, 75 grade A, none independently verified. Vercel lists TypeSafe as a second provider for Jev. Access unchanged. No agent, plugin or hook installed or run; no Jev call.
